subject: Midpilot slate safety buffer request and autoscale exception
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Midpilot slate: request for safety buffer

Hi Soojin / Kim,

Quick ask ahead of the EchoHealth midpilot next Monday: product would like a dedicated safety margin on the pilot GPU slice to avoid cold-start latency regressions during the first 72 hours. Forecast attached (pilot_traffic_forecast.csv) — expected peak concurrency 180 concurrent sessions, median seq length ~512 tokens, bursty arrival pattern near day-of launch.

What we need: a 20% safety buffer carved out of the dedicated pool attached to the pilot (model: rw-large-quant). Duration requested: 10 days (pilot + immediate stabilization).

Why: last-minute model runtime variability caused a couple of 500s in the beta run; product wants headroom to avoid user-facing errors and time to tune batching/kv cache warm-up.

Can ops/infra confirm if this is viable and whether we need an autoscale policy exception or a temporary priority band?

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal PM, Dedicated Pilots
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Midpilot slate: request for safety buffer

Thanks Laura — looping infra/ops. A few clarifying questions so we can scope the ask:

- Which exact model variant will you pin to (rw-large-quant or rw-large-fp16)?
- What p99 latency SLO are you targeting for the pilot (and are you willing to accept a fallback model variant if capacity runs short)?
- Is the 20% buffer against the entire dedicated pool or just the pilot slice (i.e., do you want global isolation or a soft-priority band)?

Marcus / Dev — can you sketch short feasibility? If we require an autoscale policy exemption, please indicate duration and rollback criteria.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Midpilot slate: request for safety buffer — ops feasibility

Short feasibility note:

- Current dedicated pool (us-west) utilization: baseline 65% with scheduled reserved slices; ephemeral free capacity ~14 GPUs today after planned maintenance window on 1/22.
- For rw-large-quant (4 vGPU per replica equivalent), the 20% headroom Laura requests translates to ~12 GPUs for the pilot at peak; that's above ephemeral free capacity.

Options I recommend:
1) Approve a temporary 15% buffer carved as a soft-priority band (non-preemptive for 10 days). This requires an autoscale exception for the pilot slice to bypass normal eviction rules for the first 72 hours.
2) If product insists on strict 20% isolation, we must either defer one low-priority reserved slice (manual reassign) or secure burst capacity from our cloud partner (extra cost + 24–36h lead).

Operational constraints / rollback: grant exception window of 72 hours for non-preemption; after 72h, automatic re-evaluation via monitoring and load tests. Failure criteria: sustained p99 latency above 1.5x target for 2 consecutive hours or cluster pressure > 92%.

I've attached an ops runbook stub (ops_runbook_midpilot.md) with steps for carving the soft band and instrumentation checklist. If approved, I'll open INF-4821 and a temporary policy change ticket.

[Attachment: ops_runbook_midpilot.md]
—Marcus

Couple of notes from product policy / finance lens:

- If we apply a temporary dedicated carve with an autoscale exemption, we need written product lead approval (Laura) and infra sign-off (Marcus). Finance needs to be looped for any marketplace/cloud burst costs.
- Suggested approval path: Product lead email thread approval -> Infra ops ticket (INF-4821) -> Billing notification to finance@redwood.com -> PM/Account exec to confirm any contractual communications with EchoHealth.

Also: please ensure we record the exception in the pool stewardship ledger and include a cost estimate. Marcus, can you provide the cost delta for the cloud burst option in the runbook?

Thanks,
Kimberly

Subject: Re: Midpilot slate: request for safety buffer — APPROVED (15% soft band)

Decision: approved with adjustments.

- Approve a 15% soft-priority band for the EchoHealth midpilot (10-day window: 2026-01-25 to 2026-02-03).
- Autoscale policy exception granted for the first 72 hours (2026-01-25 00:00 PST through 2026-01-28 00:00 PST). After 72 hours, automatic reversion unless Marcus flags continued instability.
- Marcus to create INF-4821 and the temporary policy change ticket; add the monitoring hooks in the ops_runbook_midpilot.md.
- Kimberly will notify finance and record the exception in the stewardship ledger; Laura to confirm product acceptance of the 15% (not the 20% initially requested).

Next steps / owners:
- Marcus: create INF-4821 and attach runbook + cost delta (due: 2026-01-23 18:00 PST)
- Kimberly: finance notification and ledger entry (due: 2026-01-24 EOD)
- Dev: implement the autoscale exemption toggle and the rollback automation (due: 2026-01-24 EOD)
- Laura: confirm acceptance of 15% buffer with EchoHealth and update pilot runbook (due: 2026-01-24 EOD)

Thanks everyone — tagging a 30m sync for Monday 2026-01-25 08:30 PST to monitor day-one.

Attachments: policy-exception-form.pdf
